sources_considered.why: Original, pre-publication version of a controlled complexity study.
Tests whether tool use changes the original study's findings.
Replication identifies both persistent failures and important experimental qualifications.

evidence_items.locator: Abstract, results of controlled puzzle experiments
evidence_items.explanation: Supports the complexity-related error claim in the tested puzzles. It does not establish that errors are fatal to practical agents.
Tool-assisted results caution against treating unassisted puzzle failures as an intrinsic limit on agents. Relative improvement does not itself establish reliable autonomous work.
Some apparent complexity failures depended on unsolvable test configurations. The agent pairs here are puzzle participants, not deployed AI agents.

unresolved_gaps: The evidence supports complexity-related failures in particular settings, but does not establish a universal relationship across tasks and agent designs.
No defined reliability threshold or representative evaluation establishes that error accumulation prevents useful autonomous work.
The studies do not isolate step count from every other source of task difficulty.
